request: Please find me data regarding first-of-class ship cost overruns

reply.reply:
**Recent Ford-class data show program unit costs rose 3% (about $480 million) year over year, while the FY2026 budget requested $150.0 million to cover cost growth on the ship scheduled for delivery in March 2027.**

- GAO reported Ford-class program unit costs were up 3 percent, or about $480 million, year over year; about half of the increase was attributed to CVN-79 schedule changes, with the remainder including CVN-80 delays and cost increases on later ships. (RS20643, PDF p. 19)
- The FY2026 budget estimated the ship’s procurement cost at $13,196.0 million and requested $150.0 million to cover cost growth on it. (RS20643, PDF p. 8)
- LPD-17 Flight II's unit procurement cost targets were $1,643 million in constant FY2014 dollars for the lead ship and an average $1,400 million for ships 2 through 11. (R43543, PDF p. 8)
reply.reasoning: I found current CRS coverage citing GAO’s 2025 assessment of Ford-class cost growth and specific FY2026 cost-growth funding for a Ford-class ship. A separate amphibious ship report provides lead-ship cost targets for context, but not an overrun figure.
